title: Make a flow say the digits
brief: Build sway sampling, the masked infilling loss, classifier-free guidance with batched passes, CosyVoice's chunk mask, and a mel pseudo-inverse, then train a conditional flow-matching model that generates spoken digits you can hear.
hints: sway works on numpy and torch alike if you pick the cosine function by type: torch.cos for a tensor, np.cos otherwise.
In infilling_batch, reshape t to (B, 1, 1) and the mask to (B, 1, N) so both broadcast over the bands.
masked_flow_loss divides by mask.sum() * F, not by the number of elements, so a clip with few masked frames still gets a fair loss.
In sample, one call per step on torch.cat([x, x]) with torch.cat([cond, null_cond]) gives both velocities; split the result with [:B] and [B:].
chunk_causal_mask is one broadcast comparison: (j // c)[None, :] <= (i // c)[:, None].
np.linalg.pinv(filterbank) @ mel_power can go negative between filters; clip at 0 before the square root.
